thread:
deploy-bot: Started rollout r2026.03.15-11 to eu-west canary group A (10% traffic)
jen wang: seeing p95 go from ~120ms -> ~1.8s for model/serve-34 on canary nodes :thinking_face:
oncall-bot: paging @mike_sre (incident: high-latency-canary) :rotating_light:
mike_sre: on it, grabbing logs and metrics
jen wang: queue depth on serving proxy increased, batch sizes collapsed to 1-2 ops, throughput down ~60%
alex_r: grep on runtime logs shows repeated "kernel_select: falling back to generic_attention_kernel" around deploy start time
mike_sre: that suggests the optimized kernel path is missing/invalid for the compiled artifact. could be mismatch between kernel build flags and new runtime handshake
jen wang: also seeing continuous KV cache misses on same hosts, weirdly correlated to kernel fallback spikes
mike_sre: pulling metric snapshots: p50 140ms -> 200ms, p95 1200ms -> 1900ms, error rate 0.6% -> 2.8%
mike_sre: linking graphs: https://grafana.company/shot?panel=serve-34-canary (copied)
maya_pm: any customer impact yet?
cassie_cs: Zendesk ticket 84732 — timeout errors for embeddings endpoint for a handful of customers, flagged as P2. They're seeing 500s and long tails. Updating customer with "we're investigating"
jen wang: deploy-bot shows canary at 10% still. we can either let it failfast or flip the feature flag to opt back to old batching path. prefer kill-switch to avoid full rollback initially
mike_sre: agree. flag name is feature:batched_dispatch_v2. toggling that will keep binary but route to legacy dispatcher. lower blast radius
jen wang: running flag flip now
```bash
# disable new batching on canary group
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  https://ops.console/flags/feature:batched_dispatch_v2/disable \n  -d '{"scope":"canary-group-A"}'
```
deploy-bot: Flag disable accepted for scope canary-group-A — change propagated to 10 hosts (2s latency)
mike_sre: seeing batch sizes climb back up, queue depth stabilizing
alex_r: kernel_select fallback logs dropping off on canary nodes, looks like optimized kernel path now being used again
jen wang: tail latency improving, p95 down to ~350ms within 4 minutes of flip
mike_sre: still seeing a few hosts with intermittent fallback; prepping a rollback for canary revision r2026.03.15-11 -> r2026.03.15-10 just in case. scheduling now
deploy-bot: Initiating rollback to r2026.03.15-10 for canary group A
jen wang: note for postmortem: suspected root cause = build artifact compatibility mismatch (kernel codegen flags) + new batching exposing edge-case in kv cache warmup leading to transient cache misses
cassie_cs: notified impacted customers: "we mitigated the issue by disabling the new batching feature and rolling back canary, full rollback if we see reflow." Customer-facing note drafted, sending now
maya_pm: please capture timeline + who flipped flag + artifact ids and exact hosts for the RCA. Also include the support ticket numbers and SLA exposure assessment
alex_r: handing off to night oncall @mike_sre-night (I need to step off) — summary: canary caused kernel fallback + batching collapse, mitigated by feature flag flip and rollback; customer impact limited to a small set, CS notified. logs + artifacts saved to /incidents/2026-03-15/1767778000/
mike_sre: taking handoff, will monitor for 2 hours then escalate if regressions reappear. I'll watch kernel_select events and p95 tails
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-42 — summary "canary deploy induced kernel fallback and batching regression". Pager duty: primary @mike_sre, secondary @alex_r
cassie_cs: updating ticket 84732: "We implemented a mitigation and rolled back the canary. Our engineers will monitor and follow up with RCA."
mike_sre: next steps: (1) preserve canary hosts for deeper debugging, (2) verify new artifact build flags and run compat matrix, (3) add a pre-rollout check that validates kernel signatures before traffic shift
jen wang: adding immediate postmortem note in #postmortems and creating eval run to reproduce with synthetic traffic
maya_pm: thanks team. please leave any remaining logs/commands here before handoff completes
jen wang: copy — leaving traces: kernel binary id = sha256:aa11bb22cc33, build flags: -O2 -fno-fast-math, runtime expects -Ofast; attaching to incident folder
alex_r: ack, offboarding now. good job team :thumbsup:
mike_sre: monitoring. will update incident channel with any changes
deploy-bot: Rollback complete for canary group A — traffic back to r2026.03.15-10
jen wang: closing thread for active ops; keeping incident open for RCA.
